formula: 100 x transfers out of CBP(t) / children in CBP custody(t)
columns: Children transferred out of CBP custody; Children in CBP custody
unit: % of reported CBP custody per reported day
frequency: Daily; period value is pooled: 100 x sum(transfers) / sum(custody snapshots)
denominator: Same-day reported snapshot (default). Option: previous snapshot, only when it is exactly one day earlier. Whether the snapshot is opening or closing is undocumented.
missing: NaN when custody is 0 or missing, or transfers missing. Never 0 or infinity.
interpretation: Descriptive: transfer activity relative to the reported custody population. Higher values mean more transfers per child reported in custody.
limitations: Not a transfer probability and not a processing time. Values above 100% are possible because custody is a point-in-time snapshot while transfers accumulate over a day. Unavailable where CBP values are screened out.

formula: 100 x discharges from HHS care(t) / children in HHS care(t)
columns: Children discharged from HHS Care; Children in HHS Care
unit: % of reported HHS care population per reported day
frequency: Daily; period value pooled as for TSR
denominator: Same-day reported snapshot (default) or one-day-earlier snapshot.
missing: NaN when HHS care is 0 or missing, or discharges missing.
interpretation: Descriptive: discharge activity relative to the reported HHS population.
limitations: Not a placement success rate. HHS describes discharges as children 'united to a vetted sponsor' but publishes no categories or counting rules, and the data do not track cohorts. The children discharged are not necessarily those in the denominator.

formula: mean HHS care / mean daily discharges over the period (= 100 / pooled DSR)
columns: Children in HHS Care; Children discharged from HHS Care
frequency: Weekly, monthly, quarterly, or selected period
missing: NaN when there are no discharges in the period.
interpretation: How many days of discharges at the current pace the reported population represents. Under a steady state (Little's law) it approximates mean time in care.
limitations: Not a measured length of care. Biased whenever the population is growing or shrinking, which is most of this dataset.

formula: CBP stage: sum(transfers)/sum(intake). HHS stage: sum(discharges)/sum(transfers). System: sum(HHS discharges)/sum(CBP intake). All x100.
columns: Intake, transfers out of CBP, HHS discharges
frequency: Weekly, monthly, quarterly, or selected period
denominator: Entries to the stated boundary over the same reported days as the exits
missing: Only records where both flows are present are used.
interpretation: Above 100%: more exits than entries on reported days (stock drawn down). Below 100%: entries exceed exits (stock builds). The system ratio counts the internal CBP->HHS transfer only once.
limitations: System ratio ignores CBP exits other than transfers (none are reported). HHS stage assumes transfers out of CBP are the HHS admissions. Unreported days are excluded from both numerator and denominator.

formula: stock(t) - stock(previous report); per-day version divides by the gap in days. Period change: closing snapshot - previous period's closing snapshot.
columns: Children in CBP custody; Children in HHS Care
missing: NaN if either snapshot is missing or screened out.
interpretation: Growth or reduction in the reported population.
limitations: Snapshots only; the change mixes entries and exits. The combined CBP+HHS population is not a count of unique children.

formula: CBP: intake - transfers. HHS: transfers - discharges. Window ratio: sum(entries)/sum(exits) over a trailing window.
denominator: Exits over the same records (ratio form)
missing: Records with any missing component are excluded from the window sums.
interpretation: Positive / ratio above 1: entries exceed exits on reported days.
limitations: Flows on unreported days are unknown. CBP stock-flow does not reconcile even on consecutive days, so CBP imbalance is indicative only.

formula: Per stage: sustained stock growth rule AND (configurable: OR) entries-exceed-exits rule, both evaluated on the trailing window.
unit: flag (true/false) per record; episodes of 5+ consecutive flagged records
frequency: Daily evaluation over a trailing window
missing: Not evaluated (NA) when the window has too few reported days.
interpretation: Flags potential operational pressure for review.
limitations: Not a verified queue length or waiting time; does not identify causes.

formula: Coefficient of variation = std / mean of daily discharges, over a trailing window or a calendar period; plus month-over-month % change of mean daily discharges.
missing: Needs at least the configured number of reported days.
interpretation: Lower CV = more consistent discharge activity.
limitations: Day-of-week reporting patterns inflate daily variability; CV is unstable when mean discharges are very small (e.g. late 2025).

formula: Any configured rule (see Bottleneck Detection) firing for 5+ consecutive records; alert tier = number of rules active at once (equal weights).
missing: Rules are not evaluated on insufficient data.
limitations: Rule-based screening, not proof of a delay; causes require other evidence.

formula: HHS care(t) - HHS care(t-1) + discharges(t), one-day gaps only
columns: Children in HHS Care; Children discharged from HHS Care
missing: NaN across reporting gaps or missing values.
interpretation: HHS-side estimate of admissions that does not rely on the CBP columns.
limitations: Derived, not reported. Equals admissions only if the stock-flow identity holds with no other adjustments.
